description: HermesProxy - connection proxy that lets modern WoW Classic clients play on legacy Vanilla/TBC/WotLK emulator cores (VMaNGOS, CMaNGOS, TrinityCore)
notes: This is the Xian55 fork, not WowLegacyCore/HermesProxy: the original has been dormant since v3.x (October 2023), the fork ships 4.x releases almost daily and adds WotLK Classic 3.4.3 -> 3.3.5a support. The proxy's own startup update check still polls the original repo, so it never fires here - scoop update is the update path.

The 'hermesproxy' command is not a shim of the exe: the proxy resolves appsettings.json, CSV\ and everything it writes against the CURRENT DIRECTORY, not the exe location, so a plain shim dies with 'Configuration file not found' from anywhere but the app folder. Install writes a two-line hermesproxy.ps1 next to the exe that cd's into the app folder, runs HermesProxy.exe with your arguments and cd's back, and scoop shims that. The one side effect: a relative --config path is resolved against the app folder, so pass an absolute one.

appsettings.json is persisted as a hard link, so set ClientOptions:ClientBuild and LegacyServerOptions:Address/Port/Build right in the file next to the exe. Editors that rewrite the file in place (Notepad, VS Code) keep the link intact; one that saves via a temp file and rename splits it from the persisted copy and the edit is lost on the next update. When a release adds new keys the newer defaults land beside it as appsettings.json.original - diff the two, the persisted copy never picks them up on its own.

AccountData\ is persisted too: per-account state the proxy keeps between sessions - last character, character list order, quests marked with !qcomplete, collection favorites and the account data cache. Logs\ and PacketsLog\ (binary .pkt captures of every packet, on by default via DiagnosticsOptions:PacketsLog) are deliberately not persisted; they pile up inside the version folder and go away with scoop cleanup.
